title: Carrots, canned, reduced sodium, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots cooked in vegetable oil with reduced sodium are a ready‑to‑eat vegetable product. The carrots are sliced, blanched, and then sealed in oil with a small amount of salt to preserve flavor and extend shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned carrots retain most of their beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
Cooking in oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K and vitamin E.
Reduced sodium makes the product more suitable for people monitoring their salt intake.
Carrots are one of the oldest cultivated vegetables, grown for over 5,000 years.
Canning allows carrots to be stored for several years without loss of taste.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted in the body to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and potassium help regulate blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Vitamin C and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fiber promote healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Improves nutrient absorption
items.content: The added oil increases the bioavailability of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even with reduced salt, the product still contains sodium, which should be considered in low‑salt diets.

items.title: Caloric density from oil
items.content: Added vegetable oil raises the calorie count of the product.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to carrots; discontinue use if symptoms appear.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some canned foods may contain additives or preservatives that can cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, stews, or used as a side dish. They can also be gently warmed in a pan or microwave if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated in a sealed container and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors, discoloration, or mold.
